text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 1) How Can We Improve Pagination Consistency and Efficiency?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The problem: Traditional pagination uses "give me page 2, page 3..." with an OFFSET. But in a

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: live news feed, new articles arrive constantly. If you're on "page 2" and 5 new articles arrive,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: everything shifts down you might see the same article twice or skip some. Annoying!

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The solution: Keyset Pagination (also called cursor-based pagination).

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Instead of asking for "page 2," the app says: "Give me the next 20 articles that come after the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: last one I saw." It uses the last article's timestamp or ID as a bookmark (a "cursor").

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > No duplicates, no skips, even as new articles pour in.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Much faster, because the database can jump straight to the bookmark instead of counting

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 2) How Do We Achieve Low Latency (< 200ms) Feed Requests?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Pre-compute feeds: Instead of building the feed when the user asks, we build it ahead of time

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: and store it in a fast in-memory cache like Redis.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - CDN (Content Delivery Network): Store popular content on servers physically close to users

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: around the world, so data travels a shorter distance.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 3) How Do We Ensure Articles Appear Within 30 Minutes of Publication?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Smart polling frequency: Poll high-volume publishers (like major news sites) very often (every

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: minute or two); poll smaller blogs less often.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Streaming pipeline: As soon as a poller finds a new article, it flows immediately through Kafka →

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: parser → database, rather than waiting for a scheduled batch job.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Prioritization: Breaking-news sources get checked most frequently.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 4) How Do We Handle Media Content (Images/Videos) Efficiently?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Key principle: Don't store the actual heavy files — store the links and let a CDN do the heavy

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - We store only the URL of an image/video, plus maybe a small thumbnail.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Heavy media is served through a CDN so it loads fast worldwide.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Lazy loading: Images load only when they're about to scroll into view, saving bandwidth.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 5) How Do We Handle Traffic Spikes During Breaking News?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Auto-scaling: Automatically add more servers when traffic surges, then remove them when it

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Aggressive caching: During breaking news, everyone wants the same top stories — so one cached

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Load balancers: Spread incoming requests evenly across many servers so none get overwhelmed.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Rate limiting: Gently cap abusive or excessive requests to protect the system.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 6) How Can We Support Category-Based Feeds (Sports, Politics, Tech)?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Tag every article with one or more categories during the parsing step. This can be done using

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: keyword rules or a machine-learning classifier (a program that learns to sort articles into topics).

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Store the category as a field in the database.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The API then accepts a filter, e.g., GET /api/v1/feed?category=sports, returning only matching

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - We can pre-build a cached feed per category for speed.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 7) How Do We Generate Personalized Feeds?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - This tailors the feed to each user's interests based on their behavior.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Track signals: Which articles a user clicks, how long they read, what topics they favor.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Build a profile: "This user loves tech and sports, ignores politics."

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Rank accordingly: A ranking algorithm scores candidate articles higher if they match the user's

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Content-based filtering → "You read tech articles, so here's more tech."

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Collaborative filtering → "People similar to you liked these, so you might too."

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Personalized feeds are usually pre-computed in the background and cached, keeping them fast to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Aggregating a feed of news articles from thousands of global publishers.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Enabling users to "infinitely" scroll through the news feed.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Allowing users to click on an article and be redirected to the original publisher's website.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Availability over Consistency: The system should almost never go down. If a user sees a

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: news article that's a few minutes old (slightly "stale"), that's totally fine. Nobody is harmed

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: if a headline shows up 2 minutes late. So we prefer "always on" over "always perfectly up-to-

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Low Latency: When a user opens the app, the feed should load in under 200 milliseconds

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: (that's faster than a blink). New articles should appear in feeds within 30 minutes of being

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Say each article (text + metadata like title, author, URL) is about 50 KB.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > 10 million articles/day × 50 KB = 500 GB per day.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Over a year: 500 GB × 365 ≈ 180 TB per year.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Incoming (pulling articles from publishers): 500 GB/day ÷ 86,400 seconds ≈ 6

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Outgoing (sending feeds to users) is much larger because of the read-heavy nature —

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: potentially gigabytes per second at peak.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > 100 million users, each refreshing their feed ~10 times a day = 1 billion reads/day.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > 1 billion ÷ 86,400 seconds ≈ ~11,500 QPS on average, with peaks several times higher.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Think of the system as a box. What goes in, and what comes out.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > RSS/Atom feeds (explained in detail below — this is the main one!)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > News APIs (some publishers offer direct data feeds)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Web crawlers (programs that visit websites and read their content)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > A clean, ranked news feed delivered to the user's phone or web browser through an API.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Pollers/Crawlers regularly check publisher RSS feeds for new articles.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > New articles are dropped into a message queue (like Kafka) — a waiting line that keeps

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Parsers clean up the data (extract title, text, image, source URL).

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Cleaned articles are saved into the database.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > User opens the app → request hits the API Gateway.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The feed service fetches and ranks articles from the database.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The ranked feed is returned to the user — fast.

g.text: Google News is a digital service that aggregates and displays news articles from thousands of publishers worldwide in a scrollable interface for users to stay updated on current events.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Imagine every news website had a standardized notice board where they automatically post

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: a short summary every time they publish a new story. Instead of you visiting 10,000

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: websites to check for news, each site keeps its own tidy list that any program can read.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - That "standardized notice board" is called an RSS feed (RSS stands for Really Simple

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - An RSS feed is just a special file (written in a format called XML) that lists recent articles.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: An RSS feed is designed for computers to read — it's plain, structured, and predictable.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Polling = regularly re-checking each RSS feed (e.g., "every 5 minutes, look for new items").

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Crawling = a program that visits webpages and reads their content directly. Used when a

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: publisher doesn't offer an RSS feed.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Be respectful: good crawlers obey robots.txt (a file where sites say what's allowed) and

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: don't hammer servers too fast. Learn more from Google's crawling documentation.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Aggregated Feed → The ingestion pipeline (pollers → queue → parsers → database)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: continuously gathers articles from all publishers into one unified collection.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Infinite Scroll → We use keyset pagination (explained below) so each scroll loads the next

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Redirection → Each article stores the original source URL. When tapped, the app opens
